    Why did the Rockets lose Game 7?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    The Houston Rockets lost Game 7 to the Golden State Warriors primarily due to poor offensive execution, especially in the paint and from three-point range, combined with the Warriors' veteran leadership and key performances from Stephen Curry, Jimmy Butler, and Buddy Hield, who exploited Houston's defensive lapses and capitalized on opportunities the Rockets couldn't finish. Key issues included a lack of physicality in finishing at the rim, getting stagnant against the Warriors' zone defense, missing crucial free throws, and an overall inability to match Golden State's clutch performance in the fourth quarter, where the Warriors' stars shone. 
    This video breaks down the key reasons for the Rockets' loss in Game 7:
    1m
    KHOU 11
    YouTube · May 5, 2025
    Offensive Struggles:
    • Poor Shooting:
      The Rockets shot poorly, particularly from deep, attempting only 18 threes and making few, failing to generate enough offense from the perimeter. 
    • Paint Inefficiency:
      They missed numerous close-range shots in the paint (23/55), failing to convert easy opportunities. 
    • Zone Defense Issues:
      The Warriors' zone defense caused stagnation, and the Rockets struggled to make the right reads or knock down open shots. 
    Warriors' Star Power & Experience:
    • Stephen Curry & Jimmy Butler Dominance:
      Curry and Butler provided the scoring punch and veteran presence needed in crunch time, with Curry taking over in the fourth quarter. 
    • Buddy Hield's Spark:
      Hield was a surprise factor, hitting crucial shots and outperforming the Rockets from beyond the arc. 
    • Draymond Green's Leadership:
      Green's energy and playmaking as a catalyst were vital for the experienced Warriors squad. 
    Watch this video to see why the Warriors' stars were so dominant in Game 7:
    55s
    Basket Junkies
    YouTube · Jun 1, 2018
    Execution & Effort:
    • Missed Free Throws:
      The Rockets missed critical free throws, a recurring theme in their losses during the series, indicating a lack of composure. 
    • Lack of Second/Third Efforts:
      They were outworked on loose balls and second-chance opportunities, allowing the Warriors to extend plays and get kick-out threes. 
    In essence, the Rockets' youth and inexperience showed as they couldn't consistently execute against a veteran team, leading to offensive frustration and costly mistakes in the decisive game.

      Why do Lakers jerseys have 44 on them?
      The No. 44 on the Lakers' jerseys honors the great Jerry West. West, who died at the age of 86 in June, spent much of his NBA life as part of the Lakers' franchise. The man whose likeness became the NBA's logo was a dominant player, then a coach and executive for the Lakers over several decades.Sep 20, 2024
